kusajātaka.p: [Kusa+jātaka] (na) CL=7 Kusajātaka. A story that is based on a Bhikkhu that is when Lord Buddha dwells in Jetavana monastery, a Bhikkhu who is bored in monkhood so he wants to disrobe.
pn:
Kusajātaka (Ja 531). The story of Kusa (q.v.). It was told in reference to a backsliding monk who fell in love with a woman in Sāvatthī, neglected all his duties and refused food. He was taken to the Buddha, who related this story to show how even mighty men may lose their power and come to misery through love of a woman. (Ja.v.278ff; the story is also given in Mvu.iii.1ff; ii.441f; the details differ, as do some of the names, from the Pāli version).

The story bears much resemblance to that of Anitthigandha (q.v.). See also Sammillabhāsinī.
a: ဘုရားရှင်ဇေတဝန်ကျောင်း၌ နေတော်မူစဉ် ငြီးငွေ့ဆန့်ကျင် လူထွက်ချင်သော ရဟန်းကို အကြောင်းပြု၍ ဟောသောဇာတ်၊ ကုသဇာတ်။
